Nutrition

No breakfast, a 16:8 fast (noon–8pm), two real meals, nothing elaborate. Target ~2,100 kcal and 150–180 g protein a day — that pace loses 1–1.5 lb/week at ~250 lb, and the protein is what protects muscle while the weight comes off.

Plan the week below by tapping foods into meals — calories and protein count themselves. The shopping list is computed from the plan minus what's already in your pantry. Everything saves automatically on this device.

Fasting rules of engagement

  • Outside the window: water, black coffee, tea, zero-cal drinks. Inside: the plan above.
  • Morning walks and core work fasted are fine — that's easy-pace work. If a strength session feels flat, slide it later, closer to the window.
  • Feeling lightheaded isn't a badge, it's data: drink water, salt your food, and if it persists — eat. The fast serves the deficit; the deficit doesn't serve the fast.
  • Weigh in mornings after the bathroom, before coffee. Log it with your coach — the chart does the judging, not the mirror.

Why this setup holds up

  • Calorie-matched, intermittent fasting and continuous dieting lose the same weight — and 16:8 shows the best adherence of the fasting protocols. Adherence is the whole game; this is the pattern you already live.
  • Fasting's one real risk while cutting is muscle. The fix is what this plan does: big per-meal protein doses across only 2–3 feedings, plus the strength work in the weekly plan.
  • Macros in the planner are per-serving estimates — close enough to steer by. The weigh-in trend is the real feedback loop; when it drifts, the coach adjusts the calorie target, not the effort.
